question.prompt: Suppose \(a\) is \(150\%\) of \(b.\) What percent of \(a\) is \(3b?\)

solutions.title: Double the given relation
solutions.explanation:
Since \(150\%=\frac32\), doubling \(a\) gives exactly \(3b\):
\[
a=\frac32b
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
2a=3b.
\]
Thus \(3b\) is twice \(a\), or \(200\%\) of \(a\). The answer is \(\boxed{200}\), choice \(\text{D}\).

solutions.title: Use convenient numbers
solutions.explanation:
Only the ratio matters, so we can use \(b=100\): changing \(b\) scales both \(a\) and \(3b\) by the same factor.

Then \(a=150\) and \(3b=300\). The requested percentage is
\[
\frac{300}{150}\cdot100\%=200\%.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{200}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
